stem: If \(y\) is a function of \(x\) and \(\log(x + y) = 2xy\), then the value of \(y'(0) =\) _______.
currentSolution:
**(D)** \(1\)

First find \(y\) when \(x = 0\). Putting \(x = 0\) in \(\log(x + y) = 2xy\),
\(\log(0 + y) = 0\) \(\therefore \log y = 0\) \(\therefore y = 1\).

Now differentiate \(\log(x + y) = 2xy\) w. r. t. \(x\), treating \(y\) as a function of \(x\) (chain rule on the left, product rule on the right),
\(\frac{1}{x + y}\left(1 + \frac{dy}{dx}\right) = 2\left(y + x\frac{dy}{dx}\right)\)

Substitute \(x = 0\), \(y = 1\),
\(\frac{1 + y'}{0 + 1} = 2\left(1 + 0\right)\)
\(1 + y' = 2\)
\(\therefore y'(0) = 1\)

currentSolution:
[Textbook note: The complete solution set is theta = n(pi)/3 (from tan(3 theta)=0), which is not among the four options. The official key B (n(pi)/6) follows from the identity tanA+tanB+tanC = tanA tanB tanC when A+B+C = n(pi), i.e. 6 theta = n(pi); it is the intended answer, though n(pi)/6 technically includes points such as theta = pi/6 where tan(3 theta) is undefined.]

The equation reduces to \(\tan\theta+\tan2\theta=0\Rightarrow\tan\theta(3-\tan^2\theta)=0\), giving \(\tan\theta=0\) or \(\tan\theta=\pm\sqrt3\), i.e. the full set \(\theta=\tfrac{n\pi}{3}\).
